blocks.text: Langley: how mobile and manufactured homes work here

items.t: The tenure frame the whole page turns on: in a manufactured home park, many tenants own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, governed provincially by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA); where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect park-home buyers

items.t: Zoning — two Langleys, kept separate: Township parks sit under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 (SSMUH Bylaw 6020, adopted Nov 18, 2024, has no six-unit tier; suite cap 120 m²; coach house is a fee-simple second unit under s.102; R-CL s.403 = 220 m² minimum lot area / 464.5 m² maximum lot area); any City of Langley property sits under City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 (adoption date not confirmed). SSMUH does not apply to pad tenancies.
Name variants for the same addresses, not different parks — verify by address, not by name.

A transfer does not re-price the pad: On an MHPTA assignment the existing pad rent and the existing next-increase date carry to the new tenant — the seller's rent history is part of what a buyer acquires, and it is documented in the tenancy agreement the seller must share before consent is sought.

faq.q: Do I own the land under a park home in this price band?
faq.a: No, in a pad-rental park. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA. Pioneer Park is the exception in form, not in land ownership: there you buy the home plus co-op shares, not land.

faq.q: Does the park raise my pad rent when I buy the home?
faq.a: No. On assignment under MHPTA s.28 the pad rent stays the same and the scheduled date of a subsequent increase does not change; assignment requires the landlord's prior written consent (or deemed consent, or an order of the director) and the landlord cannot charge a fee for consent.

faq.q: Can a park refuse me because of age?
faq.a: In a 55+ park, yes on assignment: the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Regulation recognises a park where every site is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 and allows the landlord to refuse an assignment where the proposed purchaser does not meet the park's age requirement. The strata exemptions do not automatically apply — ask the park for its rule in writing.

faq.q: What is the monthly cost stack besides the purchase price?
faq.a: In structure, not figures: pad rent under the regulated formula, plus home insurance, plus property tax on the home's assessed value excluding the land in a park, plus utilities as the specific park's agreement allocates them. No dollar figure for any element is stated here, because no official source publishes a Langley figure for any of them.

faq.q: Are there market statistics for Langley mobile homes under $500k?
faq.a: No manufactured-home statistics are published in the SnapStats report — it has no manufactured-home category. The only SnapStats figures for Langley are all-residential community context, as of September 2026: Detached median $1,345,000 (449 active, 64 sold) and Condos & Townhomes median $611,000 (699 active, 128 sold) — neither describes this page's manufactured-home shelf (community-stats-sep2026.csv (as of November 1, 2026)).
